Each fisher carries a simple weight gauge and a small ledger—either a paper sheet or a shared tablet. They record the exact weight of the fish they plan to bring in, along with the date and their name. The council runs a weigh‑in station at the dock each morning. A fisher who has caught more than the recorded weight must return the excess fish back into the lake right there; we weigh the removed portion and update the ledger. agent_4.answer:

In practice that means we mark the first day after we do the annual survey—usually the day of the village festival or the first month after the fish spawn—as the start of the season, and it runs until the same date the next year. This matches the lake’s natural cycle and keeps the rule simple for everyone.
